newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate to debate FY 1997 HUD money bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate to debate FY 1997 HUD money bill.

text.p: The U.S. Senate is scheduled to begin debate on a fiscal year 1997 funding bill for Department of Housing and Urban Development at roughly 1400 EST Tuesday.
But votes on any amendments that are offered today and on a final bill are not expected until Wednesday at the earliest, Senate staff members said.
The bill, like that of a House version approved earlier this summer, includes millions of dollars in funding for programs of interest to the municipal bond market.
They include Community Development Block Grants (CDBG), expiring Section 8 contracts, and the HOME investment partnership plan.
The House approved $4.6 billion in CDBG funds and $1.4 billion for HOME, the same levels voted by Congress in FY 1996 and the same figure cleared by the Senate Appropriations Committee on July 11.

A key issue will be controversial Senate panel language that would give HUD's secretary discretion to renew expiring Section 8 contracts for a one-year term at the current rent or comparable street rent, whichever is less.
Housing bond groups object to the provision, saying Congress should require the secretary to renew contracts rather than give the secretary discretion.

Under the provision, HUD's secretary could renew expiring contracts at rates above the current or street rent only "if such rent level would be inadequate to meet reasonable operating costs and debt service."
